sources.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.population_design_dose: 43 controlled studies; healthy adults; supervised concurrent training >=4 weeks vs identical strength alone. Chronic strength, explosive strength and hypertrophy, not next-morning readiness.
sources.findings: Pooled maximal strength and hypertrophy did not show clear attenuation; explosive-strength attenuation was present, especially close/session combinations. No universal compatibility or spacing claim follows.
sources.locator: Abstract Methods/Results; Discussion sections on explosive strength and limitations; publisher lines185-214.
limitations: Mostly medium/low methodological quality; intensity not consistently reported
Active training status pooled broadly; chronic group estimates cannot identify acute individual adequacy
counterevidence: L04 finds endpoint/subgroup attenuation under different definitions
No order-specific pooled effect established here; same-session power exception matters

sources.title: Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al.
sources.population_design_dose: 19 qualitative/13 meta-analyzed studies of runners after resistance exercise; heterogeneous strength protocols, tasks and assessment times.
sources.findings: Acute peak torque and subjective/muscle-damage measures could worsen while several submaximal running physiological outcomes showed little change. Task and dose matter.
sources.locator: Results; Discussion including protocol contrasts; limitations and practical implications, publisher lines198-211.
limitations: Too few studies for robust 6/10/24/48h recovery curve
Does not quantify cost of the exact squat/RDL/split or guarantee a reduced set restores performance
counterevidence: Some submaximal tasks not impaired; reducing every lower/run pairing is unjustified
No single protocol result can define all runners time-to-recovery

sources.title: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.population_design_dose: 137 systematic reviews of randomized healthy-adult RT interventions,6-52 weeks; literature search October2024. General strength, hypertrophy, function and power outcomes.
sources.findings: Progressive RT with goal-specific variables is supported; many configurations work. Failure is not necessary; exact optimal set counts and individual response cannot be read from pooled summaries.
sources.locator: Eligibility; Tables3/6; Discussion and limitations lines900-924. Full text newly available in this round, unlike pilot abstract access.
limitations: Review overlap quantified only for strength; variable-level overview not comparison of all compound programs
Group-level general adult evidence does not certify an individual dose, clinical clearance, or specialized concurrent/taper program
counterevidence: More volume may improve some outcomes; omitted work is not assumed equivalent
Specificity and goal change can make a convenient substitute inadequate

sources.title: Concurrent Strength and Endurance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on the Impact of Sex and Training Status
sources.authors: Huiberts RO, Wust RCI, van der Zwaard S
sources.population_design_dose: 59 studies/1346 healthy adults18-50, concurrent >=4 weeks; strength/endurance training status classified separately. Online2023, issue2024.
sources.findings: Subgroup and outcome-specific attenuation qualifies universal no-interference claims. Highly strength-trained populations were absent; female hypertrophy data sparse.
limitations: Mostly untrained strength participants; limited highly trained endurance evidence
Subgroup association does not select acute action from sex or prove female safety
counterevidence: Different definitions and endpoints fromL01; no vote-counting or same-PICO contradiction invented
Not an individual prediction or automatic priority policy

sources.title: Monitoring the athlete training response: subjective self-reported measures trump commonly used objective measures: a systematic review
sources.authors: Saw AE, Main LC, Gastin PB
sources.population_design_dose: 56 original studies comparing subjective and objective well-being measures under acute/chronic load; indexed abstract read. Full PMC challenge and BJSM403 prevented fulltext retrieval.
sources.findings: Subjective reports were generally sensitive to load; subjective and objective measures often did not correlate. Auxiliary context only.
limitations: Abstract only; never sole basis of prescriptive rule
No universal converging-flags cutoff or dose algorithm validated
counterevidence: Subjective/objective disagreement is not automatically invalid data
Monitoring sensitivity does not establish intervention efficacy

sources.title: Monitoring Training Load to Understand Fatigue in Athletes
sources.population_design_dose: Narrative review of practical athlete load/fatigue monitoring; includes elite-context examples, not an intervention trial.
sources.findings: No single definitive fatigue marker; internal/external load, protocol, context and individual longitudinal response need interpretation together.
sources.locator: Internal versus External Load; Methods6.1-6.13; questionnaires and sleep.
limitations: Narrative contextual source, ineligible as decisive prescriptive support
Some examples/technologies are older; not a proposed product biomarker algorithm
counterevidence: RPE/HR/HRV affected by protocol and environment
No guarantee monitoring improves performance or identifies clinical risk

sources.title: The Effect of Load and Volume Autoregulation on Muscular Strength and Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: Hickmott LM, Chilibeck PD, Shaw KA, Butcher SJ
sources.population_design_dose: 15 studies:6 load-autoregulation and9 volume-autoregulation; resistance-trained populations, chronic1RM and muscle CSA outcomes.
sources.findings: Autoregulated versus standardized load produced similar strength gains overall; volume/protocol endpoints varied. RIR-based estimates are subjective and can be inaccurate.
sources.locator: Results/Discussion, load and volume prescription; Primary Limitations, publisher lines247-257 and308 onward.
limitations: No universal superiority of autoregulation
Velocity-loss bins not transferable to a numerical RIR/reps progression cutoff
Does not validate the exact4-6rep/2-4RIR/2.5kg fixture envelope
counterevidence: NewerL11 abstract reaches broader superiority wording; inaccessible full methods and protocol mixtures prevent upgrading to universal claim
Preauthorized execution flexibility and target mutation are distinct product decisions

sources.title: Does Taking a Break Matter—Adaptations in Muscle Strength and Size Between Continuous and Periodic Resistance Training
sources.authors: Halonen EJ, Gabriel I, Kelahaara MM, Ahtiainen JP, Hulmi JJ
sources.population_design_dose: 55 initially eligible untrained18-40 males/females; physician health inclusion; periodic10wkRT/10wkbreak/10wkretraining vs continuous20wkRT; machine leg press and biceps curl outcomes.
sources.findings: Lost strength/size could be regained during retraining and final adaptations were similar over the studied training exposure. The trial does not test catch-up volume or establish a need for it.
limitations: Not trained concurrent runners or exact14 day pause; no restart load/volume percentage derived
Physician-screened research inclusion is not software eligibility clearance
Authors explicitly exclude applying findings to illness/injury interruptions
counterevidence: Detraining caused changes before regain; no presumption old targets remain appropriate
Specific machine/untrained outcomes do not prove barbell or running reentry dose

sources.title: Effects of tapering on performance in endurance athletes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.authors: Wang Z, Wang YT, Gao W, Zhong Y
sources.population_design_dose: 14 studies/174 athletes17-32; mainly male running/cycling; well-trained or VO2max>55 inclusion. Controlled taper trials with varied doses/durations.
sources.findings: Tapering can improve endurance time-trial outcomes; moderator estimates are not a universal taper recipe. Competition-specific and concurrent-strength doses remain individual questions.
sources.locator: Eligibility criteria; Table1; Results/Table2; Limitations and conclusion.
limitations: FewRCTs; mostly men; limited training-status comparison
Specialized well-trained endurance evidence not all recreational adults
No exact combined10 kmstrength taper validated
counterevidence: Some moderators inconsistent; no universal41-60% reduction or<=21day command
Race cancellation/postponement changes intent, not automatic restoration of old workload

sources.title: Maximizing Adaptations in Concurrent Training: An Umbrella Review of Meta-analyses
sources.population_design_dose: 17meta-analyses, 144individual studies,1492participants as reported in publisher abstract; search February2025; subscription preview.
sources.findings: Broad concurrent-training compatibility is reported; abstract acknowledges sparse highly trained/elite evidence. Used for currency/countercontext only.
sources.locator: Publisher Abstract and explicit subscription-preview label lines44-62.
limitations: Full methods/results inaccessible; not sole prescriptive support
Underlying reviews overlap; not independent replication ofL01/L04
counterevidence: Does not override endpoint-specific power or acute task findings
Abstract sequence wording cannot prove a universally preferred order

sources.title: Autoregulated resistance training for maximal strength enhancement: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
sources.population_design_dose: Networkmeta-analysis of APRE/RPE/velocity/percentage-based training; abstract and indexed selected text; PMC challenge and publisher403 blocked fulltext.
sources.findings: Authors favor autoregulated methods overall; protocol/endpoint ranking differs and abstract intervals do not support a universal superiority rule.
sources.locator: PubMed Abstract Results/Conclusions; fulltext not read.
limitations: Full-text access missing in this instance
Indirect comparisons and protocol mixtures require full-method appraisal
counterevidence: L07 did not show general load-autoregulation superiority
Neither source validates exact fixture progression thresholds

fulltext_read_depth: Selected actual Methods, Results, Discussion and limitations, not every supplement or raw study reanalysis
correction_status: No notice observed for admitted decisive sources on accessed records/searches; not exhaustive. Pilot Zhao2026 corrected review remains excluded; correction text not independently accessed.
